problem: R17 keeps the information-prefix horizontal payload-COM correction at full weight while the already-qualified hybrid law transfers support to the table. On exposed stock sh5 this leaves a four-sample counterfactual My rise at release; post-release command smoothing did not change it.
intervention: Retain the complete R17 controller and its shared estimator. Once the existing observable hybrid support handoff advances, multiply only the information-prefix horizontal COM correction by one minus the greatest hybrid_alpha observed so far. The monotone latch prevents a detached payload correction from reappearing when the handoff profile returns; hybrid_alpha is the existing C2 public-signal handoff state. No detector output, simulator force, case identity, future value, new clock, threshold, grip change or alarm suppression is read. The known box-relative COM, mass, vertical COM and all controller terms remain unchanged.
rationale: The inferred horizontal correction contributes only to the payload torque being handed from robot to table. Its additional torque model should therefore disappear continuously with the same measured-support handoff rather than survive as a distinct model state across detachment.
first_stage: Run only the already exposed stock sh5 failure. Require status ok, all four unchanged G4 clauses, every original cost <=1.05 of both R10 and raw R15, no false rise not matched within 20 ms to R10/R15/R16, protected tool delay, no additional saturation, p99 <=800 us, exactly one C2 reduction from the frozen information action, no detector or grip changes, and finite state.
second_stage: Only after sh5 passes, run exposed stock sh3 and rp1:up known-pass controls plus the remaining exposed stock normals. Require the same gates on every row. Do not open perturbation or impact holdouts on any normal failure.
impact_stage: Only after all exposed normal gates pass, replay already exposed protected single-impact comparisons with unmodified thresholds and compare the complete physics and alarms; no new holdout or tuning.
limits: This is local simulation research. Reject rather than retune after any opened outcome. R10 submission, original kit and prior evidence remain unchanged.
